Creeper World 3. I don't know how I even found it. Indie simulation-strategy, nothing else really like it.

Here's how I see it -

Neither has better design than the other since it's not as black and white as that. What they do have is advantages in different departments that give them their own edge. AAA developers have a lot of money (ideally) and people which allows them to have highly polished games that are both beautiful and full of content.

While indies are often starving, they're at much less of a risk when it comes to designing with experimental ideas. So we tend to get a lot more "interesting" or new things from indies, which in turn can lead to better game design.

But ultimately, I think beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Both are just as capable of making good design as well as bad design (and there's plenty of terrible games out there from both sides of that coin to prove it).

I see them both having great design, but in different ways.

I think the AAA studios have great design, in that they've mastered, honed, and refined the tried-and-true styles that we all know and love.

On the other hand, many indie games forge new paths, and make us stop and think about new ways to play, and connect with our tech. Discovering a new way to do something (that works) is a design accomplishment in and of itself, in my opinion.

When I read the outrage, that was the first thought that leapt to my mind as well. "This was the scene that pushed people over the top?". Of course it was an uncomfortable scene...it was supposed to be! Plus, as you note, other scenes of rape have occurred. Add to that: there's a ton of nudity, extreme violence, genital mutilation, and the list could go on. In short, I think the most vocal critics are neither fans of the show or book but people who saw a chance to become outraged.

While I can only speak for myself, I'm pretty sure that the majority of the frustration wasn't that she was young or innocent, but that it was just completely wrong for her story arc. I was yelling at the tv when it happened, not because I have an issue with depiction of rape, but because it was just lazy, wrong, and completely outside of the narrative that they had established for her. It undermined what they've been doing with her for four seasons.

And it isn't just with her. There's some lazy direction all over the place. The Arya storyline, The Sparrows, Jaime and Bronn, are all just bad in terms of narrative. But when people hate those storylines it doesn't make news because they're not hating rape. But again, it's not that rape is offensive, it's just dead wrong for her arc.

While they have changed a lot about the story from the books they really haven't shown Sansa being anything other than just a whiney brat who refuses to acknowledge what's been done to her family. With this direct action against her she begins making the transformation from brat to who she really is to become. Up until now she has sat idly by and let the world trample her and everything she knows. With her rape (because we all know Ramsay is capable) and newfound info from Reek, I beleive its time she let hell loose upon those who have wronged her just in time for Stannis to come waltzing in. So while its out of her book character, being that in the book she isn't anywhere near Winterfell, I think this story is taking a whole other shape all its own.

I haven't read the books, but have appreciated what they had done with her in the show. She starts out just wanting to be a pretty princess, even scorning her sister's toughness. Shit for her gets real when she's with Joffrey, and she starts to realize that she can't just exist and expect to survive unscathed. She really starts to get it as she travels to the Eyrie and has to deal with Lysa. There were some really excellent moments with her during that stay. When she realizes that to save her life, she has to put on the performance of a lifetime to stop Lysa from killing her. And when she became aware of Littlefinger's weakness for her, she really made a hard play to wrap him around her finger. Coming out in that black dress was a huge moment for her. That was her turning the corner, realizing that there was always a game afoot, and that you had to both listen to what people were saying and what they weren't saying. She got that people needed to be manipulated to stay ahead of the game.

And she was moving along that arc. Getting it and playing smart. And now she's just at the mercy of a lunatic. There's no politics here. There's no progress in who she is able to become. That arc that flowed naturally for four seasons has come to a dead stop and we just get a couple of episodes of her begging Theon for help. It's a train wreck in storytelling. Didn't surprise me at all to read that this wasn't in the books. Because it's the completely wrong narrative for her character.

This lunatic has caused just as much chaos in everyone's story arc as well. You could argue that Theon Greyjoy did not need to endure what he did. Her rape was there to reassert just how absolutely insane Ramsay Snow (Bolton my ass) still is and that he will destroy the world before normality ever sets in. You lose some of the fear of his insanity in the build up to Sansa's wedding after Ramsay is legitimized. He is almost nice at times. And considering how delicate they were with her scene, in that there is no nudity and no direct physical interaction is displayed, I think they went about this display with as much care as can be imagined. Even so far as making Reek watch, they really want you to absolutely hate Ramsay Snow and have no qualms about it. Before you could have said Theon was just a casualty of war, Ramsay was just trying to prove himself just like Theon, he had been cast aside so many times you could almost feel for him. But then reality came knocking. Don't get me wrong, it was rough to watch but I felt like it was just as important as the opening scene of Gladiator. Revenge is only as sweet as the deeds it has come to correct.

But I think Theon's and Sansa's arcs are very different. I felt that Sansa had a clear trajectory and there's no point in sidelining this story arc. It works against the story. Like if 20 minutes of Return of the Jedi concerned the Emperor dealing with a serious bout of constipation and visiting various Death Star proctologists. It's not that constipation doesn't happen (especially for people his age), but it serves no narrative purpose, and would greatly detract from how we perceive the Emperor as a character. It would undermine his arc quite a bit.

Theon, on the other hand, was wrapped up in reaching too far to prove himself to his family. He was willing to throw away any kind of ethical code, to sell out the people and community that have done nothing but right by him, and was way out of his league in trying to carry so much military power. His suffering at the hands of Ramsay is an appropriate downfall in that Ramsay also has no interest in ethical considerations. He kind of receives back tenfold (or like 100-fold, from what I hear about the books) what he inflicted on Winterfell. Especially given that Ramsay is basically in the same situation as Theon, trying desperately to please his dad. It's poetic.

And I'm genuinely not worked up at all that there was a rape, or whether or not it was handled well. I thought Sansa was playing the game well with Littlefinger and that she realized what was needed to get by. And that she had effectively won over Littlefinger to the point that he would be willing to just about anything for her. It was brilliant to watch (again, I've got no idea how it plays out in the books though). But this Ramsay stuff doesn't advance her at all. It was progressing so nicely! Now she's stopped. She gets beaten regularly, raped, and is basically helpless. There's no development or advancement for her in that. She's learning that bad things happen? That the world is cruel? She got a big fat does of that with Joffrey. She knows that well. Learned it a bit from Lysa and Robert too. You could throw just about any other character into that situation with Ramsay and it'd carry the same dramatic weight.

To me, it feels like everything was perfectly constructed for four seasons. Almost impossibly perfect. And this year there are inconsistencies and events that just don't make sense in over half of the story arcs. Castle Black is mostly great, and Daenerys/Tyrion is riveting. The rest feels like they kinda gave it over to the writers of Lost and said to make it sassy.

Just an opinion.
